reel_endcard.title: Sigue a @inmigraforma
reel_endcard.sub: Noticias de inmigración de EE.UU., claras y verificadas

theme: US immigration news explained in simple Spanish (and English) for regular immigrants and their families - people with no legal training who need to know what changed and whether it touches their life
voice: WHO YOU WRITE FOR: regular immigrants and their families - not lawyers, not academics. Many read Spanish as their main language, on a phone, while busy. Write like a trusted neighbour who happens to understand the paperwork, not like a law firm. Test every sentence: would a 10-year-old understand it? If not, rewrite it. SIMPLE BY DEFAULT, EVERYWHERE: short sentences (under ~15 words). Everyday words only. Never use a legal or bureaucratic term without first saying it plainly: not 'adjudica' but 'decide'; not 'beneficiario' but 'la persona que pide'; not 'presentar una solicitud' but 'mandar los papeles'; not 'vigencia' but 'desde cuándo vale'. Official names stay in English (Green Card, parole, Visa Bulletin, I-485, EAD, RFE) but ALWAYS followed by a plain explanation the first time, e.g. 'el I-485 (el formulario para pedir la Green Card desde dentro de EE.UU.)'. Prefer 'qué hacer / qué no hacer / qué esperar' framing. MANDATORY SLIDE 2 - EN PALABRAS SIMPLES: the whole news in 2-3 everyday sentences plus one concrete comparison from daily life (school, bank, bus, store, a game). Zero jargon. Slides in Spanish, plus one short English recap paragraph in the caption written at the same plain level, with an 'In plain words:' sentence. Calm, precise, neutral - never alarmist, never speculative about future policy. NEWS may come ONLY from official government outlets: uscis.gov, dhs.gov, state.gov, travel.state.gov, federalregister.gov, justice.gov/eoir - verify on the official page and name the source and date on the slide for every claim (the source line can be formal; the explanation around it must not be). Immigration-lawyer commentary may be used ONLY as clearly labelled opinion (eyebrow 'OPINIÓN', lawyer/firm named), never as news, always with the not-legal-advice disclaimer. Prefer explainers that stay accurate for at least two weeks. Never individual legal advice: every caption ends with 'Información general, no asesoría legal. Consulta a un abogado de inmigración para tu caso.' Visual style: keep the account's existing look.
cta_line: Sigue a @inmigraforma para noticias de inmigración de EE.UU. explicadas en español.
search_brief: recent US immigration policy and procedure changes from official sources — USCIS announcements, DHS and State Department notices, Federal Register rules, the monthly Visa Bulletin, court decisions affecting immigration, and analyses published by immigration lawyers
post_arc:
Each post is a 5-7 slide carousel, ALL slides in plain everyday Spanish:
  1. cover   - the news as one plain sentence a neighbour would say (not a headline in legalese); the date in the sub line
  2. step    - EN PALABRAS SIMPLES: MANDATORY, always slide 2. The whole thing explained so a 10-year-old gets it: 2-3 short everyday sentences + one concrete comparison from daily life. Zero jargon.
  3. step    - QUÉ CAMBIÓ: what changed, in plain words, then the official source (USCIS/DHS/DOS/Federal Register) and date named on the slide
  4. step    - ¿ME AFECTA A MÍ?: who this touches and who it does not, in plain words (e.g. 'si ya tienes tu Green Card, esto no te cambia nada')
  5. prompt  - DATOS CLAVE: the key dates/numbers, or a short quote of the official English text in the code box, with a one-line plain-Spanish gloss in the sub
  6. stat    - the single number or date that matters most, with 3-5 plain words saying what it is
  7. recap   - QUÉ HACER: 3-4 arrows of what to do / not do / expect, save CTA, and 'Información general — no es asesoría legal'
An OPINIÓN slide (lawyer commentary) is optional, labelled OPINIÓN with the lawyer or firm named, never the cover, always with the disclaimer.
CAPTION: news paragraph in plain Spanish; then 'En palabras simples:' paragraph (the 10-year-old explanation); then the English recap at the same plain level with an 'In plain words:' sentence.
